title: Practice 2: с-: down, and together — раз-: apart

blocks.text: Exercises: sentences from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR) and from the library's public-domain books.

exercises.q: Stones were being connected along the lines like beads on a string.
exercises.why: **сходились** is the past tense (plural) of **сходиться** (to meet, to come together; to converge, to coalesce) — imperfective; its perfective partner is **сойтись**. past: он сходи́лся · она сходи́лась · оно сходи́лось · они сходи́лись. — Wiktionary, «сходиться» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**с-, со- (+сь, +ся)** — Convergent movement from various directions towards one center. Antonym: раз-, разо-, рас- (+сь, +ся) Example: Чтобы заниматься, студентка снесла все учебники из других комнат на письменный стол. — In order to study, the student brought all her textbooks from other rooms to her desk. Дети сбежались на детскую площадь. — The children ran (from all directions) to the playground. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.; к + dat.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  The other choice: **расходились** (**расходиться**) has the prefix раз-, разо-, рас- — Divergent movement in various directions from one center.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: The priceless china shattered into fragments.
exercises.why: **разлетелся** is the past tense (masculine) of **разлететься** (to fly away, to scatter (in the air); to come apart, to be blown apart) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **разлетаться**. past: он разлете́лся · она разлете́лась · оно разлете́лось · они разлете́лись. — Wiktionary, «разлететься» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**раз-, разо-, рас- (+сь, +ся)** — Divergent movement in various directions from one center. Antonym: с-, со- (+сь, +ся) Example: Дед Мороз разнёс подарки по домам. — Grandfather Frost brought the gifts to the (various) houses. После ужина, мы разошлись по домам. — After dinner, we went to our separate homes. Prepositional phrases: по + dat. pl.; в + acc. pl.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: She wanted to get away from everyday life.
exercises.why: **сбежать** (the infinitive) (to run down (from); to run away, to make off, to flee, to break out) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **сбегать**. — Wiktionary, «сбежать» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**с-, со-** — Movement downwards. Antonym: вз- Example: После представления актёр сошёл со сцены. — After the performance, the actor got off the stage. Prepositional phrases: с + gen.; на + acc.; к + dat.; за + inst.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The prefix "с-" implies the following meanings: (a) to descend, to go down: Мы съезжаем с горы. Он сходит вниз по лестнице. (b) to come off, to drive off: Автомобиль съехал с дороги. Поезд сошёл с пути. Note that these verbs (сходить, съезжать, etc.) are usually followed by the preposition с + Gen.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  The other choice: **взбежать** (**взбежать**) has the prefix вз-, взо-, воз-, вс-, вос- — Movement upwards.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.why: **сойдите** is the imperative (вы, plural or polite) of **сойти** (to go down, to come down, to descend, to get off; (figuratively) to come off, to disappear, to go from) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **сходить**. imperative: сойди́ · сойди́те. — Wiktionary, «сойти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**с-, со-** — Movement downwards. Antonym: вз- Example: После представления актёр сошёл со сцены. — After the performance, the actor got off the stage. Prepositional phrases: с + gen.; на + acc.; к + dat.; за + inst.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The prefix "с-" implies the following meanings: (a) to descend, to go down: Мы съезжаем с горы. Он сходит вниз по лестнице. (b) to come off, to drive off: Автомобиль съехал с дороги. Поезд сошёл с пути. Note that these verbs (сходить, съезжать, etc.) are usually followed by the preposition с + Gen.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
